name: Argha Dey Web Application Recon Checklist
description: Phase-by-phase web application reconnaissance derived from the Recon & Enumeration notes. Emphasizes the Nmap -> Fingerprint -> Fuzz -> Leak -> Foothold chain used in 90% of CPENT web challenges.
examHabits: nmap's http-generator script output often reveals the exact CMS/version before running specialized scanners
Check ftp-anon in every scan — an FTP open with anonymous allows often contains backup files with creds
If the site returns the Apache default page, the real app is under a different vhost or path — fuzz for it
Use feroxbuster first (faster than gobuster/ffuf) then refine with extension-aware fuzzing
quickRef: nmap -sC -sV -T4 -Pn -A <ip> | feroxbuster -u http://<ip>/ -k -w common.txt | whatweb http://<ip>/ | wpscan --url http://<ip>/ -e vp,u,vt,cb,m --api-token <token>

decisionPoints.fallback: nmap -p- -T4 --min-rate 5000 -oG allports.txt <ip> then re-scan discovered ports with -sV

decisionPoints.action: Note exact port and banner. Look for http-title, http-server-header, http-generator
decisionPoints.fallback: Jenkins/Tomcat often on 8080/8081 — check for /script/text, /manager/html

decisionPoints.action: ftp <ip> — login anonymous:anonymous — browse for backups, creds, configs
decisionPoints.fallback: Check for shared directories with write access (upload webshell)

decisionPoints.action: Note for later CVE-based privilege escalation hunting
decisionPoints.fallback: If no version, guess from Apache/Nginx version and search for known exploits

decisionPoints.action: Try default credentials — admin:admin, root:toor, cisco:cisco
decisionPoints.fallback: Banner grab with nc -nv <ip> <port>

decisionPoints.action: App may not be on / — fuzz for vhosts and alternative paths
decisionPoints.fallback: Check Host: header fuzzing with ffuf -H 'Host: FUZZ.<ip>'
Manual version check via /readme.html or /wp-includes/version.php

decisionPoints.condition: Login page branding shows product name (OTRS, Jenkins, etc.)
decisionPoints.action: Search 'default creds <product>' + CVE for that version
decisionPoints.fallback: Check view-source for commented-out links or file paths
dirb http://<ip>/ /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/common.txt
dirb with multiple extensions enabled
Check Host header injection: Host: FUZZ -> if page changes, vhost exists

decisionPoints.action: curl http://<ip>/robots.txt — look for Disallow entries revealing hidden paths
decisionPoints.fallback: Check sitemap.xml for URLs not found during fuzzing

decisionPoints.action: git-dumper https://github.com/lianh/docem — extract git history; search for commits with secrets
decisionPoints.fallback: Manual: curl http://<ip>/.git/config — check remote URL for repo path
grep -R -i -E 'pass|secret|key|token' extracted_dir/
smbmap -H <ip> — check for null-session shares
Verify user existence via VRFY/EXPN or just proceed with user enumeration
Manual: curl /wp-json/wp/v2/users | jq for user enumeration
Searchsploit for the specific CMS version CVEs

decisionPoints.action: Set browser proxy to Burp. Enable intercept. Test every parameter with single quote, <script>, ${IFS}, |id
decisionPoints.fallback: Use Burp Intruder for quick fuzzing of interesting parameters

steps.phase: Phase 8 - Master Recon Checklist (mental, every new Web Range IP)

decisionPoints.condition: Always check these 5 things for every new web target
decisionPoints.fallback: N/A — this is the checklist itself
